filename: Adult Male Verbal Communication Research - Deep Research Report.md
analytical_strengths: Highest-rigour report in the corpus. Explicit five-level evidence hierarchy; explicit confidence tiers; repeatedly refuses to convert usage into psychology.
principal_limitations: Uses citeturn-style inline reference tokens that cannot be resolved to URLs from the file alone; effect sizes are reported but not independently verifiable here.

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: Second, differently-generated report on the same brief. More assertive, more archetype-driven, less hedged. Adds Precarious Manhood, Gender Similarities, Talk Club, Norwich City/Samaritans, CALM, Men's Sheds, F1 team radio.
principal_limitations: States campaign outcomes (7,500 contacts; 161 lives saved; 63% attribution) that are campaign-reported and uncontrolled. Presents archetypes as findings. NOT independent of S01 at the study level - substantial shared underlying literature.

filename: Riset Komunikasi Pria Dewasa Indonesia - Deep Research Report.md
analytical_strengths: Highest-rigour Indonesian communication source. Maintains the usage/preference/effectiveness distinction throughout. Excellent pronoun and address map. Explicitly states that no Indonesian randomised wording experiment was found.
principal_limitations: citeturn tokens unresolvable; Indonesian corpus is brand-heavy and Jakarta-weighted.

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: Rich local detail: Gudang Garam and Extra Joss copy, MS Glow For Men, Kahf, AyahASI, Menyala Abangku, discourse particles, class/generation register mapping.
principal_limitations: Presents several psychological claims (e.g. a BPS 20%/40% help-seeking split) that are not traceable to a primary source in the document. Archetypes and register-by-class claims are asserted, not measured. Overlaps heavily with S03.
use_in_this_synthesis: SECONDARY; USE FOR LINGUISTIC AND CORPUS DETAIL, NOT FOR EFFECT CLAIMS

filename: Global Manosphere Research Study - Deep Research Report.md
analytical_strengths: Very high rigour. Explicit STRONG/MODERATE/EMERGING/WEAK labelling per conclusion. Explicitly separates exposure, membership, belief, and violence. Contains the corpus's best boundary framework (MCCF).
principal_limitations: citeturn tokens unresolvable; incel over-representation acknowledged by the report itself.

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: Adds the Inverted Iceberg framing, a twelve-dimension subcommunity comparison, the guru-arc and commercial-funnel models, and an Indonesia/SEA section with local names (Hitman System, Pria 100%, Hijrah Masculinity).
principal_limitations: Asserts a '2-5% of exposed audiences' escalation figure and several protective-factor claims without traceable sourcing. States the commercial incentive to maintain insecurity as established when S05 rates it EMERGING/WEAK.

filename: Indonesian Manosphere Research Project - Deep Research Report.md
classification: A. Final report - LOWEST RELIABILITY IN CORPUS
analytical_strengths: Broad coverage of the intended question set and honest about evidence gaps in several sections.
principal_limitations: Contains garbled or non-existent Indonesian ('banjir receh', 'HP mewek', 'Sunan awali maharim', 'CEWEK-ngan: Reseek!'), invented-sounding hashtags, and multiple unsourced assertions. Several 'findings' are the author's inference stated as observation. Treat every specific claim as unverified.
use_in_this_synthesis: USE ONLY FOR QUESTION FRAMING; DO NOT CITE FOR FACTS

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: By far the most useful Indonesian ecosystem source: named creators and platforms, the local lexicon (bucin, mapan, melek realita, pria berkualitas, cowok lembek), the legal/religious/adat codification of provider duty, BPS-cited structural statistics, a six-country SEA comparison.
principal_limitations: Statistics are cited second-hand and must be verified against primary BPS releases before publication. Illustrative creator quotations are reconstructed, not verified transcripts. No audience-effect measurement anywhere.
use_in_this_synthesis: PRINCIPAL SOURCE FOR DESCRIPTION; NOT FOR EFFECT CLAIMS

filename: Masculinity Framing Research Synthesis - Deep Research Report.md
analytical_strengths: The single most methodologically disciplined document in the corpus. Systematically separates masculinity labelling, targeting, prescription and threat; insists on the negative-control question; identifies the behaviour-vs-label divergence hypothesis; contains the Indonesian null finding and the Indonesian lexical gap analysis.
principal_limitations: Its central conclusion is an absence of evidence, which is correct but limits directly actionable guidance.

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: Adds the Real Men Real Depression brochure evidence, the NZ latent profile analysis, the Haslop classroom resistance study, the Scholz vegan-framing null, the job-ad debiasing evidence, and an Indonesian lexical register table.
principal_limitations: Repeatedly states as established what S09 rates as insufficiently evidenced (e.g. that men 'frequently' support behaviours while rejecting masculinity labels). Some effect-size cells are image placeholders and therefore unreadable.
use_in_this_synthesis: SECONDARY; ITS UNIQUE STUDIES (esp. Real Men brochure) ARE VALUABLE AND HAVE BEEN RETAINED

filename: Organizational Moral Communication Research - Deep Research Report.md
analytical_strengths: Very high rigour. Explicitly dismantles the '30% moral density rule'. Separates moral loading, density, emotion, outrage, conviction, grandstanding and virtue-signalling attribution. Contains the petition virality/conversion dissociation.
principal_limitations: Almost entirely US/Western political and commercial contexts; explicitly states there is no Indonesian moral-density evidence.

classification: A. Final report (independent second generation, same brief)
analytical_strengths: Adds a six-level outcome hierarchy, platform-by-platform analysis, and - uniquely - Indonesian moral-communication cases (Unilever Pride 2020 backlash; MUI Fatwa 83/2023 boycotts with PLS-SEM evidence that religious authority outweighed brand image).
principal_limitations: States the '25-35% inflection point' more confidently than S11 permits. Several causal claims (e.g. Gillette's $8bn write-down) are attributed more strongly than the evidence supports. Platform tables are largely assertion.
use_in_this_synthesis: SECONDARY; ITS INDONESIAN CASES ARE THE UNIQUE CONTRIBUTION

classification: A. Final report with an explicit verification pass
analytical_strengths: Unique in the corpus: it documents its own fact-checking, issues two explicit corrections to a prior draft, and carries a five-tier certainty hierarchy including an 'unverified' tier. Contains the anti-shaming intervention evidence and the loneliness-epidemic correction.
principal_limitations: Concerns a documentary and its reception as much as science; several reviews and figures are flagged by the report itself as unconfirmed; advocacy-organisation data is prominent and non-peer-reviewed.
use_in_this_synthesis: PRINCIPAL SOURCE FOR INTERVENTION AND CERTAINTY-CALIBRATION EVIDENCE

filename: Dissertation_ Masculinity, Social Conditions, and Mental Health in Indonesia.md
classification: A. Primary academic work (MSc dissertation, Critical Interpretive Synthesis)
domain: D7 Indonesia masculinity, social conditions and mental health
analytical_strengths: The only peer-supervised primary academic study in the corpus and the only source that systematically integrates masculinity, social conditions and mental health for Indonesia. 154 studies read against 6 Indonesian studies. Authored by a member of the Menungsa team (named in the acknowledgements), supervised at the University of Edinburgh, developed with Relational Ground LLC.
principal_limitations: Interpretive rather than aggregative by design; only six Indonesian studies exist to read against; Javanese and Muslim-weighted, as the author states explicitly; two of the six Indonesian studies are not men-only; no primary data collected.
use_in_this_synthesis: PRINCIPAL SOURCE - HIGHEST WEIGHT FOR INDONESIA
